I'm 64 now, and it's just me working these 6 mu. My wife passed a few years back and my children are working in Shijiazhuang, so I don't have family labor to call on anymore. Forty years I've farmed this land, so I know every corner of it. The maize stubble is cleared and it's time to get the winter wheat in the ground — I'll start planting around October 12th, same as I have for decades.

For wheat, I'm sticking with the improved Jinmai variety I used last year. I got about 450 kg/mu, which was decent. The extension agent told me 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is enough, but I've always done closer to 18 kg and it works for my soil. I'll put down a base dressing of compound fertilizer before planting — about 40 kg per mu — then topdress with urea at jointing in March if the wheat looks a bit yellow. At my age, I can't afford a bad harvest, so I'd rather apply slightly too much than too little. Better to waste a few yuan on fertilizer than lose half my yield.

Pumping from the well costs money, and electricity isn't cheap. I'll irrigate the wheat three times: once right after planting to help it settle in before winter, once at green-up around March, and once at flowering if the spring stays dry. My neighbor Zhang runs four irrigations, but he has a bigger farm and more cash in hand. Three is enough if the rains cooperate.

The real headache is labor. Planting 6 mu by myself at 64 is tiring. For wheat planting I can manage over three or four days, but come June, the window between wheat harvest and maize planting is barely a week. I'll hire the custom combine for wheat harvest — they charge about 60 yuan per mu — and I'll probably hire two local guys for a day to help me get the maize seed in quick after the wheat comes off. 

For the summer maize, everyone around here plants Zhengdan 958 hybrid. You have to buy hybrid seed every year, can't save it. I'll put down about 16 kg N per mu, split between base fertilizer at planting and a urea dressing at the jointing stage. If July and August are dry, I'll irrigate twice; if the rains come, maybe only once. I'll budget for twice to be safe.

I always keep a couple thousand yuan aside for medicine and emergencies, so I watch my spending carefully. Total input costs will run me about 4,500 yuan for both crops. If things go okay, I should get around 450 kg/mu of wheat and 480 kg/mu of maize. That's enough to fill my own grain jars, sell a bit, and get by another year.
